gh-dial.label: The dial
gh-dial.map: The dial by the Chiapothecary door

garden-door.label: The garden door
garden-door.closed: The garden's for another day. You can see most of it from here.

plant-lavender.label: Lavender
plant-lavender.moment: Run your hand over it and you'll smell it for hours.

plant-rosemary.label: Rosemary
plant-rosemary.moment: Tough as old boots, this one. It stays green all winter.

plant-thyme.label: Thyme
plant-thyme.moment: Tiny leaves, lots of flavour. A sprig goes in nearly every soup I make.

plant-sage.label: Sage
plant-sage.moment: Soft as felt. Fry a few leaves in butter and you'll see why I grow it.

plant-mint.label: Peppermint
plant-mint.moment: Peppermint. It lives in its own pot, or it takes over everything.

plant-balm.label: Lemon balm
plant-balm.moment: Lemon balm. Crush a leaf and it smells of lemon sherbet.
moments: The bees find it before I do. I leave them a corner of it.
A few leaves in a jug of cold water is all I do with it.

plant-basil.label: Holy basil
plant-basil.moment: Holy basil, tulsi. Peppery, a bit like cloves. Lovely as a tea.

plant-chamomile.label: Chamomile
plant-chamomile.moment: Pick the flowers when they're fully open, and dry them for tea.

plant-calendula.label: Calendula
plant-calendula.moment: Pot marigold. The petals go in salads, and in balm for dry hands.

plant-echinacea.label: Echinacea
plant-echinacea.moment: The bees love it, and I leave the seed heads on for the birds.

plant-borage.label: Borage
plant-borage.moment: The flowers taste a bit like cucumber. Freeze them in ice cubes.

plant-fennel.label: Fennel
plant-fennel.moment: A few fennel seeds after dinner. My nan swore by it.

plant-ginger.label: Ginger
plant-ginger.moment: Ginger, in a deep pot. You lift the roots in autumn.

plant-turmeric.label: Turmeric
plant-turmeric.moment: Ginger's cousin. Same idea: the good part's under the soil.

plant-aloe.label: Aloe vera
plant-aloe.moment: Thick, cool leaves full of gel. Mind the edges, they're spiky.

plant-roselle.label: Hibiscus
plant-roselle.moment: Roselle. The red calyces make a sharp, ruby-red tea, hot or iced.

passionflower.label: Passionflower
passionflower.moment: It's been trying to lift the roof off for years.

nettle-bed.label: The nettle bed
nettle-bed.moment: Nettles, in a bed of their own. Gloves on. The young tops make a good soup.

seedlings.label: Seedlings
seedlings.moment: Whatever comes up gets potted on. Eventually.

seed-packets.label: Seed packets
seed-packets.moment: Next year's planting, if I remember where I put them.

drying-herbs.label: Drying herbs
drying-herbs.moment: Bunches drying for the winter: lavender, rosemary, sage, whatever's spare.

wind-chime.label: The wind chime
wind-chime.moment: It rings when someone opens the garden door. Mostly that's me.

garden-view.label: The garden
garden-view.moment: The herb garden, then the wall, then the sea.

spring.label: Spring
spring.moment: Spring. Everything's in a hurry to grow.

summer.label: Summer
summer.moment: Summer. The bees have found the borage.

autumn.label: Autumn
autumn.moment: Autumn. Time to lift the ginger and hang up more bunches.

winter.label: Winter
winter.moment: Winter. Just the tough ones now: rosemary, thyme, sage and the aloe.

atoms.title: Pasta with sage brown butter
atoms.hook: Butter cooked until it smells of hazelnuts, with sage leaves frying crisp in it. Toss the pasta through.
atoms.method_short: Cook the pasta. Melt the butter until it foams and turns golden, add the sage leaves for a minute, then toss through the drained pasta with lemon and pepper.

seed.name: Pasta with sage brown butter
seed.why: Sage from the Conservatory, fried crisp in butter.

atoms.body: Cook the pasta. Melt the butter until it foams and turns golden, add the sage leaves for a minute, then toss through the drained pasta with lemon and pepper.

atoms.title: Crispy potatoes with rosemary
atoms.hook: Potatoes roughed up, roasted hot with olive oil, garlic and rosemary until the edges crackle.
atoms.method_short: Parboil the potatoes, drain and shake them to rough the edges. Roast in hot olive oil with garlic and rosemary until crisp, then salt.

seed.name: Crispy roast potatoes with rosemary
seed.why: Rosemary stays green all winter, and so does this.

atoms.body: Parboil the potatoes, drain and shake them to rough the edges. Roast in hot olive oil with garlic and rosemary until crisp, then salt.

atoms.title: Lavender shortbread
atoms.hook: Butter, flour and sugar, with a pinch of dried lavender rubbed in. Go gently with it.
atoms.method_short: Rub the lavender into the sugar. Beat with soft butter, work in the flour, press into a tin and bake low until pale gold.

seed.name: Lavender shortbread
seed.why: A pinch from the drying bunches is plenty.

atoms.body: Rub the lavender into the sugar. Beat with soft butter, work in the flour, press into a tin and bake low until pale gold.

atoms.title: Strawberries with lemon balm and honey
atoms.hook: Strawberries with torn lemon balm and a little honey, with thick yoghurt on the side.
atoms.method_short: Halve the strawberries. Tear over the lemon balm, drizzle with honey and leave ten minutes. Serve with yoghurt.

seed.name: Strawberries with lemon balm
seed.why: It smells of lemon sherbet, and it suits berries.

atoms.body: Halve the strawberries. Tear over the lemon balm, drizzle with honey and leave ten minutes. Serve with yoghurt.

atoms.title: Lemonade with borage flower ice
atoms.hook: Homemade lemonade over ice cubes with blue borage flowers frozen in them.
atoms.method_short: Freeze borage flowers in ice cube trays. Stir lemon juice and sugar until it dissolves, top up with cold water and pour over the ice.

seed.name: Lemonade with borage flower ice cubes
seed.why: The flowers taste a bit like cucumber.

atoms.body: Freeze borage flowers in ice cube trays. Stir lemon juice and sugar until it dissolves, top up with cold water and pour over the ice.

atoms.title: Shaved fennel and orange salad
atoms.hook: Fennel sliced thin, oranges cut into rounds, olive oil and a few olives. Crisp and bright.
atoms.method_short: Shave the fennel as thin as you can. Peel and slice the oranges. Lay them together, scatter olives and fennel fronds, then oil and salt.

seed.name: Shaved fennel and orange salad
seed.why: Fennel and oranges are both good in the cooler months.

atoms.body: Shave the fennel as thin as you can. Peel and slice the oranges. Lay them together, scatter olives and fennel fronds, then oil and salt.

atoms.title: Garden leaves with calendula petals
atoms.hook: A bowl of soft salad leaves with orange calendula petals scattered over and a lemony dressing.
atoms.method_short: Wash and dry the leaves. Whisk oil, lemon and salt, toss the leaves through, then pull the petals and scatter them on top.

seed.name: Garden leaves with calendula petals
seed.why: Pot marigold petals go in salads.

atoms.body: Wash and dry the leaves. Whisk oil, lemon and salt, toss the leaves through, then pull the petals and scatter them on top.

atoms.title: Nettle and potato soup
atoms.hook: The young tops of nettles, wilted into a potato and onion soup. Bright green, and no sting once cooked.
atoms.method_short: With gloves on, pick and rinse the young nettle tops. Soften onion in butter, simmer potatoes in stock until tender, add the nettles for two minutes, then blend.

seed.name: Nettle and potato soup
seed.why: The young tops make a good soup. Gloves on.

atoms.body: With gloves on, pick and rinse the young nettle tops. Soften onion in butter, simmer potatoes in stock until tender, add the nettles for two minutes, then blend.

atoms.title: Iced hibiscus tea
atoms.hook: Dried hibiscus flowers steeped into a sharp, ruby-red tea, sweetened with honey and poured over ice.
atoms.method_short: Pour boiling water over the dried flowers and steep ten minutes. Strain, stir in honey, cool, and pour over ice with orange slices.

seed.name: Iced hibiscus tea
seed.why: Roselle makes a sharp, ruby-red tea, hot or iced.

atoms.body: Pour boiling water over the dried flowers and steep ten minutes. Strain, stir in honey, cool, and pour over ice with orange slices.
